references.text: Moses had already told the people to gather twice as much on the sixth day, because there would be no manna on the seventh day, the Sabbath.
The Lord's response to the people's disobedience in going out to gather manna on the Sabbath, and the confirmation of the Sabbath commandment.
The fourth commandment to keep the Sabbath holy, which the people broke by going out to gather manna on the seventh day.
Another example of breaking the Sabbath commandment in the wilderness, where a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath.
The repetition of the Sabbath commandment in Deuteronomy, emphasizing the importance of resting on the seventh day.
The book of Hebrews speaks about the Sabbath rest that remains for God's people and urges them to enter that rest and not fall into the same disobedience.
Contrast between the absence of manna (judgment on disobedience) and the absence of the body (evidence of resurrection).
